text.p: The board of Highlands Gold Ltd said it maintained its unanimous recommendation that shareholders reject the 75 cents a share takeover offer by Canadian mining giant Placer Dome Inc.
"The directors of Highlands remain strongly of the view that Highlands' assets are worth significantly in excess of 75 cents per share," the company said .
None of the directors intend accepting Placer's offer for his own shares, it said.
Highlands also said it was continuing discussions with potential underwriters of a proposed restructuring plan.
Placer Dome had given Highlands until last Friday to find underwriters for the restructuring plan but Highlands was unable to do so.
Placer Dome said on Friday its offer was final and it had withdrawn its offer to buy Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea (PNG) for A$316.1 million.
It also said its offer price would not be raised.

Highlands' proposed underwriting was to raise A$160 million at 30 cents a share and was necessary to enable the Highlands group restructure, which included a new company Highlands Pacific Ltd being created to own its non-Porgera assets.
Through a scheme of arrangement, each Highlands share not held by Placer would be cancelled in exchange for a capital return of 65 cents a share and a new share in Highlands Pacific.
The new company would have held all of Highlands Gold's non-Porgera assets.
These include stakes in the Ramu nickel/cobalt and Frieda/Nena copper/gold projects and as well as an exploration portfolio and database in Papua New Guinea and Indonesia.
In Monday's statement, Highlands said its proposal to restructure the company was designed to unlock the underlying value of its assets.
"The proposal was well received by the investment community, but underwriting was unsuccessful in the limited time available," Highlands' managing director Ian Goddard said.
"The directors believe that the proposed restructure is in the best interests of all shareholders and should be pursued," Goddard said in a statement.
"Directors are therefore continuing discussions with potential underwriters," he added. He gave no details.
Highlands said its board considered it unlikely that Placer would receive sufficient acceptances for it to compulsorily acquire outstanding shares. This threshold is 90 percent.
Placer now holds more than 40 percent of Highlands.
Highlands shares fell three cents to 75 cents on Monday.
